question: Should OpenClaw add a public sub-agent pre-timeout grace/warning contract, and if so should it be global config, a per-`sessions_spawn` override, or both?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but adding a warning deadline changes public config/tool semantics and requires cross-runtime lifecycle choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Add global and per-spawn warning controls
options.body: Expose a documented default plus per-spawn override, schedule a child-visible warning before hard timeout, and test native plus ACP behavior.

options.title: Add only a global default
options.body: Keep the tool API smaller by configuring the grace period only under sub-agent defaults, at the cost of less per-task control.

options.title: Defer in favor of post-timeout recovery
options.body: Keep the current hard-timeout and recovery model and close or narrow this request if maintainers do not want child-visible timeout warnings.

recommendation.title: Add global and per-spawn warning controls
recommendation.body: Expose a documented default plus per-spawn override, schedule a child-visible warning before hard timeout, and test native plus ACP behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and prior review context place this account closest to sub-agent lifecycle, ACP spawn, and timeout/announce behavior.
